english: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be real numbers such that $\alpha-\beta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ and $\cos\alpha+\cos\beta=\dfrac45$. Then the value of $\cos(\alpha+\beta)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $\alpha$ तथा $\beta$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं जिनके लिए $\alpha-\beta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ तथा $\cos\alpha+\cos\beta=\dfrac45$ है। तब $\cos(\alpha+\beta)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: So $\cos\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}=\dfrac45$, and $\cos(\alpha+\beta)=2\cdot\dfrac{16}{25}-1=\dfrac{7}{25}=0.28$ (the sign of the half angle does not matter)
solution_full: The pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ is not unique (the half angle can be $\pm\cos^{-1}\dfrac45$ plus multiples of $2\pi$), but every choice gives the same $\cos(\alpha+\beta)$.
originality_note: New: with alpha - beta = 2pi/3 the factor cos((alpha-beta)/2) equals 1/2, so the sum of cosines IS the cosine of the half-sum (way 4, hidden simplification). Closest known: 'cos a + cos b = p, sin a + sin b = q, find cos(a+b)'. Different because: only one sum is given, and the fixed difference replaces the second equation.

concept_use.Sum-to-product and product-to-sum transf: cos alpha + cos beta = 2 cos((alpha+beta)/2) cos((alpha-beta)/2) converts the data into cos((alpha+beta)/2) = 4/5.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, function and interval is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that cos(alpha+beta) is the same for every admissible pair, so the answer is unique. Changed: No change.
key_step: Sum to product with cos(pi/3) = 1/2, then the double-angle step.
justification: Two routine steps with a small observation, numerical. Like 2021-P1-Q18 (L2).
